name: Isolated Distal Symphalangism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Symphalangism

criteria.description: Clinical evidence of fusion of distal interphalangeal joints with limited or absent joint mobility
Radiographic confirmation of bony ankylosis at distal interphalangeal joints
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other syndromic causes of symphalangism or joint fusion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical and radiographic evidence of distal interphalangeal joint fusion with exclusion of other syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for NOG gene mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: Radiographs showing bony fusion of distal interphalangeal joints
Absence of joint space at affected distal interphalangeal joints
genetic: Mutations in NOG gene (encoding noggin protein) associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Physical examination revealing fixed flexion deformities of distal interphalangeal joints

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of multiple interphalangeal joints beyond distal
Presence of conductive hearing loss more common
Additional skeletal anomalies such as tarsal coalition
Shortening of middle phalanges rather than fusion
No bony ankylosis of distal interphalangeal joints

redFlags: Progressive joint ankylosis beyond distal interphalangeal joints
Presence of systemic features suggesting syndromic involvement
Early onset severe functional impairment of hands
references: Klopocki E, et al. Distal symphalangism: clinical and molecular analysis. Am J Med Genet A. 2007
